rows.title: Jovic vs Eala
rows.tournament: US Open R3, outdoor hard (Arthur Ashe Stadium, night session opener, roof available)
rows.headline: Jovic has beaten Eala three times in 2026 and her first-strike, serve-led game travels to hard
rows.analysis: US Open R3, Ashe night opener Saturday 7pm ET (23:00 UTC; Kalshi's 18:00 is wrong). Books have Jovic about 54% (-133/+107); rankings are near-equal (#14 v #18). The direct evidence points to Jovic: 2-0 this year with dominant margins, including 6-2 6-2 on grass at Queen's when Eala was in form (she beat Swiatek three weeks later), plus a 6-3 exhibition set on this exact court nine days ago. The mechanism repeats: Jovic takes the ball early, out-hits Eala from the baseline (34-15 and 26-12 winners) and attacks Eala's weak serve, while her own serve is clearly better (67% first-serve points won, 5 aces v Frech). Eala's 2026 hard-court ledger shows the same vulnerability to flat power righties: blown out by Noskova, Muchova, Bencic (4-6 0-6), Gauff, Alexandrova and Anisimova. The counter-case is real: hard is Eala's best surface (25-10), her DC title run over Pegula, Svitolina and Osaka gives her much stronger hard-court transitive chains, Elo favours her, and Jovic's summer hard results were soft (lost to #89 Korneeva and Bouzkova, 26 UE v Jones). Night conditions and an elite return help Eala too. Net: Jovic about 56%, a genuine but thin lean; no medal.

Books have Paul -200 / Bublik +154 (about 61-63% Paul), and Kalshi at 0.61/0.39 matches. Paul is the better 2026 player (38-16, Houston title, Delray/Hamburg/Queen's finals, Cincinnati QF with a match-point save over Zverev), returns far better (38% return pts won vs Bublik's 34%) and is the fitter mover in 85F heat. Bublik skipped the whole North American swing so his body is rested, and he has won 80% of first-serve points in both rounds. Caveats: Bublik's two wins came against soft opposition (38-year-old Mannarino off a five-setter, Wolf back from shoulder injury), his hard-court level since February was poor (straight-set losses to De Minaur, Auger-Aliassime, Griekspoor, Hijikata, Berrettini), and Paul is 2-1 in ATP main-draw hard meetings. rows.headline: Ormaechea beat the #3 seed 6-4 6-2 as a dog; Sevcikova hasn't beaten a top-700 all year
rows.analysis: W15 Fiano Romano R16, red clay, 11:30 local. Ormaechea's #1226 badly understates her: ex-world #59, 389-220 lifetime on clay, 12-5 on clay in 2026 including qualifying into the $30k Trieste and reaching the QF, losing only to champion Ce. Two days ago she beat 3rd seed Gennaro (#918) 6-4 6-2 as a 2.43 underdog on these exact courts. Sevcikova (#947, CH #708) is 20-18 in 2026, but 8 wins came at a non-ITF Czech UTR series; her sanctioned record is ~12-14 and clay is 9-9. She has beaten nobody inside the top ~700 all year and is blown out at that tier: 2-6 1-6 Barbulescu (#690), 0-6 2-6 Safta, 1-6 1-6 Vogt, 1-6 2-6 Zucchini. Ormaechea beat that same Barbulescu, the [2] seed, 1-6 6-3 7-5 on clay in July. Sevcikova self-describes as a serve-and-forehand aggressor with chronic back trouble; slow Italian clay versus a career Argentine clay grinder is the wrong matchup, and she needed three sets to beat #1448 qualifier Valente. Books: Ormaechea 1.58 / Sevcikova 2.24 (58.6% vig-free). I make Ormaechea ~65%.

rows.analysis: W35 Kursumlijska Banja R16, outdoor clay, 11:00 local. But the 2024 match came when Cakarevic was ~150 spots the better player, so the live evidence is one qualifying match five weeks ago, played after Milovanovic had sat idle 18 days. Since Aug 9 both have contested the SAME four events on the SAME courts: Milovanovic 7-3 - qualified at a W75, beat #291 Kaji at a W50, lost two tiebreaks to the eventual finalist; Cakarevic 3-3, crushed 1-6 1-6 by #640 Golovina, wins only over qualifying-level opposition. The Kuzmova (#278) chain also favours Milovanovic. Offsetting: Milovanovic played the last match of the day (17:45 start, 6-3 1-6 6-3 over #1434 Virc) and returns at 11:00; Cakarevic won in ~62 minutes from 12:50. Dry, 29C, no rain. rows.analysis: Books have this 1.84/1.84 -- a true coin flip -- because Cvetkovic's maiden W35 title (Verbier, Aug 30, beating Okutoyi #488 and Strakhova #525) is fully visible against Martinez Cirez's four straight 1R exits. Two things the price doesn't carry. First, every match of that 10-1 run came at Verbier, 1,500m in the Alps: thin air, fast livelier clay that flatters her big forehand. Kursumlijska Banja is a ~450m Serbian valley -- heavy, slow clay, exactly where Martinez Cirez won all 7 of her ITF titles and reached the 2025 WTA125 Vic final (bt Tomljanovic 6-4 7-6(2), Cocciaretto 6-1 6-3). Second, the load: 12 matches in 16 days, a Verbier-to-southern-Serbia travel day Aug 31, a 3-set doubles Sep 1, singles Sep 2, doubles again at 15:30 today. Martinez Cirez has played twice in 15 days and skipped doubles. Common opponents lean Spain too. Cvetkovic is the better trajectory and is home; Martinez Cirez is the better player in these specific conditions with fresher legs.
